title: One reply from the character's language model
description: The one shape ai_llm accepts. A game narrows it to the discourse acts it declared -- an `anyOf` of this shape once per intent, each naming its intent and only its own arguments, or the empty one every intent may carry (LlmValidator.json_schema, gameaikit.llm.validator.json_schema) -- and hands that to a runtime that can constrain its output. A convenience: the validator checks every reply anyway, including the rules a schema does not say (no secret) and the ones a runtime may not hold it to.

speech.description: What the character says: one line, no markup. The pattern says the same -- no control character (C0, DEL or C1), no line or paragraph separator, U+2028 and U+2029, and no format control (Unicode's Cf, by range: T139), the last two written here as JSON escapes so the pattern holds the characters themselves (T129) -- for a runtime that constrains its output, and also leaves out the quote and the backslash: llama.cpp reads a pattern against the string's JSON text, escapes and all, and drops maxLength beside one, so the length is in the pattern too (T116).

intent.description: Which of the game's declared discourse acts the player's words were.

argument.description: One of that intent's declared values, or empty.
